newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks drift lower at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks drift lower at open.

text.p: Australian shares drifted lower at the opening on Thursday with local traders unconvinced by Wall Street's bullish performance.
By 10.25 a.m. (0025 GMT), the Australian All Ordinaries index was four points lower at 2,731.0.

Brokers said the unenthusiastic response to U.S. closes and a stronger bond market had surprised, with local investors apparently sceptical about U.S. markets and cautious as they awaited the flood of local profit results.
"Our market obviously doesn't believe New York," said broker Kevin Lourey of Melbourne-based Peake Lands Kirwan.
"The fundamentals don't support the present (U.S.) market and that is the way people are looking at it."

The upcoming rush of June 30 profit results was also causing some concern. "The results are probably going to be the next signal people will be looking to," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank.

Gaming machine maker Aristocrat Leisure Ltd plunged 37 cents to A$2.50 (US$1.88) upon reinstatement before regaining some ground to be 21 cents lower at A$2.66. Traders said concerns about the company's Colorado licence renewal refusal had provided the selling impetus.
Also on the downside, grocery retailer and wholesaler Davids Ltd dived 15 cents to a record low of 85 cents before climbing back to 91 cents.
The company on Wednesday announced a A$262 million writedown and restructured senior management. Since hitting a 1997 high of A$1.82 Davids shares have halved in value.
The leaders were slightly weaker generally in choppy trade. Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about six to five, while about 39 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
